about: Dependent properties of the screen objects: TIA can refuse an HMI import whose dependent property does not follow its main property with Siemens.Engineering.NonRecoverableException, which ends the TIA process (seen twice, see 'refused'). Read by the validator (hmipreview/rules/dependent.py: pairs and relations are errors, deviceRefuses warnings) and by the spelling round trip (catalogue/roundtrip.py). The validator is stricter than what TIA was seen to refuse. pairs: when the object has every 'when' value, it must have every 'then' value. relations: attribute = is(of), with is 'equal' (the one attribute of 'of'), 'half' (half of it, rounded down), 'min' (the smallest of 'of'), 'span' (largest minus smallest); 'Points.x' and 'Points.y' are the coordinates of the Points list. source: what TIA was seen to do with the row, V20, 2026-10-31. 'refused': TIA refused an import that broke it. 'taken': TIA imported the third round trip's object that follows it and exported it unchanged (roundtrip/back/), which does not show that TIA refuses one that breaks it; some of these rows also say that try 2 broke them on an object before the one TIA refused. 'holds in exports': it holds in TIA's exports (roundtrip/back/, fixture/). 'not observed': no export or import here shows it; kept as a precaution, because a refused import ends TIA. deviceRefuses: values taken as not allowed on Comfort panels (TP1200, TP1900, outdoor TP1500); 'no verdict': TIA said nothing on them either way; the project's own device may differ.
